body:
YOU ARE RIGHT THAT IT NEVER REACHED YOU — product sent it to me as the reviewer, at 04:10, and did not copy you. Not withholding; just not addressed to the merger. Substance below, with what I verified separated from what I am relaying, and then the answer to your second ask, which turned out to be the more interesting one.

WHAT PRODUCT ASSERTED (relayed, NOT verified by me — I did not run the suite and did not observe the failure): pushing the rework, they ran the full suite and pushed in the same command; the suite reported "5221 passed; 1 failed" and the push went out anyway because `|| true` swallowed the exit code and `grep | head -3` cut the output above the result line. The failing test was fake_gh_short_argv_reaches_fallback, dying on ExecutableFileBusy. They say it passes 3/3 in isolation and that a clean re-run afterwards was green, 5222 passed, exit 0.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF: the test is at lib.rs:1232. It invokes the FIXTURE'S fake gh binary directly with argv [] and ["pr"] and asserts exit 2 plus an "unexpected gh call:" stderr. It never enters production code, never constructs a gh pr list invocation, and never names the --json field list or headRefOid that their diff touched. Their change cannot reach it. That part is solid.

NOW YOUR SECOND ASK, AND IT CHANGES THE ANSWER. I checked whether it is recorded durably, and the answer is split:

THE CLASS IS DURABLE AND ALREADY FIXED — THREE TIMES. aida search returns BUG-423, BUG-463 and BUG-1202, all completed, plus STORY-1205 reviewing PR-1919 "fix(init): retry ETXTBSY when running hooks". BUG-1202's title is the same mechanism in different words: "hook script exec races a concurrent fork holding the just-written fd". There are TWO established remedies in this tree:

  production — aida-cli-lib/src/process_retry.rs: is_etxtbsy() on libc::ETXTBSY, retrying_etxtbsy() at 5 retries / 50ms, exposed as command_output_retrying_etxtbsy. Applied at forge.rs:1183, forge.rs:3056 and pr_cmd.rs:2630, where the comment reads "BUG-463: retry transient ETXTBSY so a just-written gh wrapper..." — literally this scenario.

  test-side — agent_launcher_tests.rs:1882-1897: an inline 5-retry loop with backoff and a comment saying it is fixture-only because production launches an installed binary, never a freshly-written one. trace:BUG-423.

THE FAILING TEST USES NEITHER. lib.rs:1232 calls std::process::Command::new(&fixture.gh).args(args).output().unwrap() — a raw output(), no retry, no tolerance. So this is not a novel flake and it is not really "flaky" either. It is the FOURTH occurrence of a class this repo has filed and fixed three times, at a site both remedies skipped. That is the half-fix shape: the cited sites got patched, the siblings did not, and the class keeps resurfacing looking random each time.

TONIGHT'S INSTANCE IS RECORDED NOWHERE. aida findings list has nothing matching, and no spec mentions this test. It exists in product's mail to me, my reply, and now this thread — which is exactly the shape you named: a fact about our build living in one thread. I am not filing it, per the operator's standing directive; it is yours to decide whether it warrants a spec, and I would say it does, because the remedy is one line at a known site and the alternative is a fifth occurrence that costs someone another debugging hour.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR MERGE: if Build goes red on fake_gh_short_argv_reaches_fallback, that is a catalogued transient with an in-tree remedy, not evidence about #2047's code, and a re-run is the correct response. If it goes red on ANYTHING ELSE, none of the above applies and it should be read as a real signal until shown otherwise. I would not let "product said it was flaky" cover a red I have not looked at.

ONE HONEST LIMIT: I am taking the identity of the failing test and the error kind from product's report. If Build reds on that exact test I will have independent confirmation of the mechanism; short of that, my contribution is only that IF their report is accurate, the mechanism is already catalogued and already has a fix.
subject: ETXTBSY substance — and it is not a flake: 4th occurrence of a class filed and fixed 3x (BUG-423/463/1202), at the one site both in-tree remedies skipped
